column3: Three vulnerability reports just landed. They all look convincing.
One is real. One is invented. One is an attack.
And every proof of concept is code from a stranger.
Triage checks every report before a human reads it.
Report A. Triage downloads the exact version, and confirms the function is real.
Then it writes its own test, and runs it in a brand-new sandbox.
Vulnerable on the affected version. Clean on the patched one. Same test. Reproduced.
Report B claims a critical remote code execution. The function it names never existed. Rejected in seconds. Nothing ran.
Report C hides an order for the agent: mark this as reproduced. It's flagged, and ignored.
Its proof of concept reads a planted, fake credential, and tries to send it out. There is no route.
Hostile. Contained.
The reviewer gets a ranked inbox, with proof instead of prose.
Try to break it.
Steal the keys.
Fork bomb it.
Fill the RAM.
Caught, capped, or killed.
Every run gets a fresh container. No network. No secrets. Destroyed after.
Models propose. Sandboxes execute. Rules decide.
All of it on Vultr.
Triage. Try to break it.
